findings.description: `_load_ideology_catalog_cooperative()` passes `true` as the finished flag when checking a newly started request, so the helper treats its initially null result as a completed load failure. findings.description: `_load_ideology_catalog_cooperative` starts a threaded load through `loading_resource_request.gd` but never checks `request.start_error` or `request.result`; once `request.finished` is true it unconditionally returns `IdeologyCatalogScript.load_default()`, which performs a synchronous `ResourceLoader.load` of the same catalog. When the threaded request fails or yields null, the country initializer quietly takes this second loading path with no `push_error`, so the failure never reaches the log and the rest of economy setup proceeds as if the catalog loaded normally.
findings.title: Failed ideology catalog load silently falls back to a sync load

citations.citation: Keynes: errors fail loudly instead of falling back silently

evidence.explanation: The previous code returned null when the threaded load did not reach LOADED, and the new code drops that failure branch. `start_error` and `result` are never inspected, so a failed load is replaced by a synchronous reload of the same resource without any logging, which is the silent switch of code path that rule 4948321 forbids.

findings.description: After each weather LUT publication, `_upload_curtain_instances` rewrites the whole compacted draw set one instance at a time. That is two `MultiMesh.set_instance_*` server calls per instance per layer, about 7.9k instances on day 30, and `_refresh_curtain_instances` also walks every map cell in GDScript first. Before this change the upload ran once per map; now it runs on each sim-day publication, and on desktop or blend boundaries the work is multiplied by layers and repeated, so phones get a periodic main-thread frame spike, worse during fast-forward.
findings.title: Weather publications re-upload every curtain instance

evidence.explanation: The idle check looks only at camera and input state. It ignores whether the clock is running or how fast. The worker is gated on the main thread finishing each day's tail work, and that work is driven per frame. The PR's benchmark notes confirm that no more than one day settles per draw. A lower frame rate therefore directly lowers simulation throughput, and mobile auto now defaults to this adaptive mode.

findings.description: The new early return `if host._runtime_climate_writeback_last_day < commit_day: return` drops the polled commit whenever the writeback cursor did not reach the commit day. `_apply_climate_writeback_if_authoritative` only advances that cursor when the native result reports `applied` (at least one field written), so a snapshot that is consumed without writing any fields (missing slots, or a slot with the wrong type or size) leaves the cursor behind for good, and every later call returns before `simulation_committed` or the day-tail work runs.

evidence.explanation: The new guard makes consuming the commit depend on the climate cursor moving forward. The cursor moves only when `applied` is true. Natively, `applied = applied_fields > 0` after the newest snapshot has already been taken from the ring. So once a snapshot is consumed with zero fields written, no snapshot remains that could ever move the cursor to that day.

findings.description: `_upload_curtain_instances` builds a compact array of only the active instances, then calls `compact.resize(mm.instance_count * _INSTANCE_STRIDE)` before `mm.buffer = compact`. So every slot sized to the whole map goes to the render server, per layer, on every weather publication, which contradicts the comment at line 174. The render-thread upload is set by map size, not by how many cells have rain or snow, and the zero padding plus allocation is repeated each sim day, including during fast-forward.
